crime.value: Double homicide and suicide by firearm at Meadowlands racetrack. Fritzi Czechi shoots his estranged wife and her companion, then shoots himself. Central question: What triggered the violence at that specific moment after the horse race?
crime.quote: He'd killed his estranged wife and her companion with two shots and three shots respectively...He'd then turned the gun on himself

victim.value: Fritzi Czechi's estranged wife (name: Rosalind, implied) and her male companion. They are 'killable' because Fritzi's obsession with his wife and jealousy of her new relationship, combined with emotional instability and access to an illegal firearm, made them targets of his rage.
victim.quote: the woman in the wide-brimmed straw hat and eyecatching lilac pantsuit...Fritzi Czechi's estranged wife and her companion

closed_world.value: Meadowlands racetrack clubhouse and stadium during an evening of races. The crowd, confined seating areas, and immediate aftermath create a bounded social space where the crime occurs publicly among witnesses.
closed_world.quote: Meadowlands that evening...in a shady section of the stadium, at the finish line, three rows up

culprit_and_motive.value: Fritzi Czechi, estranged husband and former part-owner. Motive: jealous obsession with his wife, rage at her new relationship, and likely premeditated intent (he'd rehearsed the gun stance). The timing—after Morning Star's race—suggests a climactic moment he'd engineered.
culprit_and_motive.quote: He was looking for someone, Katie knew. The wife. Ex-wife? Rosalind...It was a stance, it was an act, Fritzi Czechi had clearly rehearsed many times in solitude

resolution.value: No investigative resolution; the crime resolves through Fritzi's suicide. Katie identifies herself to police and provides testimony. The .380-caliber pistol is traced to illegal shipments in NYC mid-1980s. The victims are dead, the perpetrator dead. Order restored only by death and police documentation.
resolution.quote: Katie identified herself to police...He'd killed them with a handgun that would be identified as a .380-caliber semiautomatic pistol

investigator.value: Katie Flanders, Fritzi's lover and unwitting witness. She experiences the crime from the stadium stands, unaware of Fritzi's plan, and becomes the primary witness and narrator of events. Her perspective dominates; police enter only after the violence.
investigator.quote: Katie identified herself to police. Katie Flanders, who'd been Fritzi Czechi's companion...she'd answered their questions, all that she knew

suspect_architecture.value: Single perpetrator (Fritzi Czechi) with no traditional suspect pool; the architecture inverts convention — the killer is the romantic lead, known from the outset to the reader but not understood as such. Motive: estranged wife and her companion; means: premeditated .380 semiautomatic; opportunity: self-arranged (he gave Katie the car keys and placed the bets to position himself).
suspect_architecture.quote: He'd killed his estranged wife and her companion with two shots and three shots respectively.

red_herring.value: The entire emotional and romantic frame of the story functions as a sustained red herring: the reader is led to interpret Fritzi's distraction, nervous drinking, envelope, and gift of the BMW as tokens of romantic ambivalence or commitment, when all are components of a premeditated murder-suicide plan. The racing tension over Morning Star further displaces suspicion onto anxiety about the horse.
red_herring.quote: Into Katie's still-shaking hand Fritzi was placing—what? An envelope? … On the front hand-printed KATIE FLANDERS.

clue_fairness.value: Multiple fair-play clues are embedded and available to the reader simultaneously with Katie: Fritzi scanning the entrance for someone (the wife); his watch worn face-inward 'as if even the exact time was a secret'; the pre-sealed envelope with her name; the car deeded to her in advance; his ashen, sweaty face after the race before any violence occurs; and his having 'clearly rehearsed' the final act.
clue_fairness.quote: He wore it turned inward, the flat oval disc of digital numbers against his pulse. As if, with Fritzi Czechi, even the exact time was a secret.

social_world.value: Working-class Jersey City milieu of old high-school networks, petty glamour, and gendered economic dependency. Fritzi sits atop a patronage hierarchy — lending money, buying uniforms, sending roses — while Katie is structurally subordinate: no last name used in introductions, no life insurance, temporary secretary job, reliant on his 'esteem.' Horse racing world layered over this: owners, trainers, jockeys, grooms each with distinct status.
social_world.quote: Fritzi introduced Katie to them by only her first name. Katie smiled, trying not to think what this meant.

alibi.value: No alibi is constructed or contested in the conventional sense; instead, Fritzi creates a false situational alibi of emotional normalcy — drinking, betting, attending the race as a loving companion — which masks his premeditated intent. His apparent preoccupation with Morning Star's race serves as cover for locating and approaching his targets in the stands.
alibi.quote: He was looking for someone, Katie knew. The wife. Ex-wife? Rosalind.

reveal_mechanic.value: The reveal is enacted rather than explained: the murder-suicide unfolds in real time before Katie's eyes with no investigator intermediary. The post-facto police confirmation (weapon traced, shots reconstructed, witnesses cited) provides forensic anchoring. The envelope and car deed function as a retroactive confession, transforming the entire preceding narrative into legible premeditation.
reveal_mechanic.quote: It was a stance, it was an act, Fritzi Czechi had clearly rehearsed many times in solitude.

media_and_audience.value: Largely absent as an explicit element; the story is tightly focalized through Katie with no press or public narrative machinery shown. The police investigation appears only briefly. The crowd's panic and witness horror gesture toward public spectacle, but the story does not develop media framing as a structural element.
media_and_audience.quote: Katie identified herself to police. Katie Flanders, who'd been Fritzi Czechi's companion.

investigator_wound.value: Katie is not a detective but functions as the story's investigative consciousness. Her wound is romantic self-deception and class-inflected longing: she persistently misreads every warning sign as evidence of love ('He does love me. This is proof!'). Her vulnerability is the need to be chosen by a glamorous man, which blinds her to the truth of what she is witnessing until the shooting begins.
investigator_wound.quote: She thought, He does love me. This is proof! … Don't fall for it. You'll be hurt.
